title: Total fractions and rational generators on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the existing small affine etale basis, induced topology, actual structure rings, and module restriction equivalence [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. For a basis chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $Q(U)=S_A^{-1}A$ with $S_A$ the non-zero-divisors of $A$. A morphism of affine etale charts over $X$ is etale, hence flat, so restriction preserves non-zero-divisors; restrict a fraction by restricting its numerator and denominator. These maps satisfy identity and composition. Define $\mathcal K_X$ by sheafifying this explicit fraction presheaf and retain the actual map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K_X$ induced by $a\mapsto a/1$. For a module $L$ let $\mathcal K_X(L)$ be scalar extension of its restriction to this basis along that map. A nonzero rational section is an isomorphism $\mathcal K_X\otimes\mathcal O_X\simeq\mathcal K_X(L)$, equivalently a generating meromorphic section. The canonical localization of a regular section is given by the scalar-extension adjunction unit. An isomorphism of lines preserves rational sections if its localized map carries the first generator to the second. A rational section is an everywhere generating regular section precisely when it is the localization of an isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\simeq L$. These definitions include the empty space and disconnected spaces.
